title: NEXORA pre-migration envelope backup
description: The full options-envelope snapshot the migration runner MUST write before its first destructive step (ADR-0014, docs/architecture/35-schema-versioning-migration.md §7). Stored under -nexora.backup.<iso> in chrome.storage.local and mirrored as a file on the Connector side, because a backup that lives only in the storage being migrated proves nothing. This document is the shape of that record; the payload is the envelope verbatim.

backupId.description: Identity of this snapshot, so a resume can tell 'the backup I already wrote' from 'a backup written by a different run'.

createdAt.description: When the snapshot was taken; also the timestamp half of the storage key.

fromSchemaVersion.description: Envelope schemaVersion read from storage at snapshot time. 2 is the legacy value shipped by the fork (omega-target/src/default_options.coffee:2 -- `schemaVersion: 2`).

toSchemaVersion.description: Version the run intended to reach. The machine-checkable rule this document enforces is a floor, not an ordering: allOf below requires toSchemaVersion >= 2, the lowest version any shipped envelope can already be at. The intent is stricter -- toSchemaVersion MUST equal or exceed fromSchemaVersion, never descend -- but JSON Schema 2020-12 cannot compare two sibling integers without an if/then pair per version, so the ordering is asserted by scripts/verify.mjs over every backup record shipped here and generalised in Phase 2 (docs/verification matrix) once the version space is enumerated.

extensionVersion.description: Recorded because the update path in omega-target-chromium-extension/src/coffee/background.coffee:32-47 compares versions, and a migration must be able to say which version wrote which bytes.

keyCount.description: Number of envelope keys captured. A backup of 0 keys is how a wipe gets recorded as a success, so the runner refuses to write a migration step against one.

contentSha256.description: Hash over the canonically serialised payload, so restore can prove it is reading what was written rather than what the quota fallback left behind.

connectorMirrorPath.description: File path of the Connector-side copy, or null when no Connector is reachable. Null is allowed only for migrations with no destructive step; scripts/verify.mjs cannot see the step list, so the runner enforces that half.

restoredAtLeastOnce.description: Whether a read-back of this backup was performed and compared during the same run. An unverified backup is a file, not a recovery plan (docs/architecture/35-schema-versioning-migration.md §7 makes the check blocking).

payload.description: The captured envelope, keys verbatim including the '+' profile keys, MINUS every key matching the backup namespace: a snapshot that contains the older snapshots contains itself recursively, so its size grows with the number of runs and restoring one would resurrect the others out of order. Not schema-checked per key on purpose: the point of a backup is to survive a migration that misreads those keys.

allOf.description: A migration only ever moves forward or stays put. Expressed here as the floor the schema language can state on its own (toSchemaVersion >= 2, the shipped legacy version); the forward-only ordering between the two fields is a sibling-integer comparison and is checked by scripts/verify.mjs against every record in examples/, with the general per-version rule deferred to Phase 2.
